summary.headline: Belrise Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR25,528 mn with EBITDA margin at 11.4%; FY26 adjusted PAT up 41% to INR5,020 mn.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated total revenue grew 12% YoY to INR25,528 mn and manufacturing revenue grew 21% to INR21,763 mn, while EBITDA rose only 5% to INR2,901 mn, with margin at 11.4%. Adjusted PAT rose 17% to INR1,290 mn, with a one-time INR94.7 mn operational loss at the aerospace and defence subsidiary absorbed in the quarter. For FY26, total revenue grew 15% to INR95,091 mn and adjusted PAT grew 41% to INR5,020 mn. Management reported new two-wheeler and exhaust/fuel-tank orders, the Chester Hall acquisition in the UK, and guidance of mid-teens growth with broadly stable margins for FY27.

segments.name: Two-wheeler and three-wheeler
segments.commentary: Contributed 83.2% of Q4 manufacturing revenue and 82.0% in FY26. Content per vehicle rose 65-70% during FY26 (management also cited 60-65% on another basis), with two-wheeler content per vehicle moving from about INR12,000 to INR20,000 including the Badve Auto Comps and Eximius merger.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: Contributed 6.2% of Q4 and 5.2% of FY26 manufacturing revenue. Suspension business currently serves two- and three-wheeler OEMs only, not PV OEMs.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.4% of Q4 and 8.3% of FY26 manufacturing revenue. CV segment grew 32% in Q4 and 35% in FY26.

segments.name: Four-wheeler
segments.commentary: Four-wheeler business grew 71% in Q4 and 37% in FY26 (transcript initially said 31%, corrected to 37% in footnote). Content per vehicle rose from about INR25,000 to INR40,000-45,000 with the H-One acquisition.

segments.name: Aerospace and defence (Belrise Aerospace and Defense)
segments.commentary: Acquired SDM (France) in Q3 FY26 and Chester Hall (UK) in Q4 FY26. Q4 carried a one-time operational loss of INR94.7 mn from startup costs, legal and professional fees and personnel costs; management expects SDM to be EBITDA positive in 2027.

guidance_outlook: Mid-teens revenue growth expected to continue, supported by the order book.
EBITDA margins expected to remain broadly stable versus FY26 levels (FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 12.1%); cost pressures seen as short-term and not expected to affect medium-to-long-term margins.
Capex expected at 6% to 6.5% of manufacturing revenue, with R&D included within this range.
Doubling four-wheeler and CV revenue versus FY25 within the current fiscal year requires about 40% to 45% growth, per management endeavour.
Final dividend of INR0.55 per share declared.
SDM expected to turn EBITDA positive in 2027 after the one-time Q4 loss.
capex_capacity: Bangalore brownfield expansion to supply exhaust systems and fuel tanks to a fast-growing two- and three-wheeler OEM; production slated to begin Q2 FY27 with peak annual revenue of INR90 crore.
Large order from a Japanese two-wheeler OEM for exhaust systems and metal components; peak annual revenue about INR220 crore, production starting Q4 FY26-27 (transcript says 'this fiscal year').
Haridwar plant ramp-up: trial parts dispatched to a large two-wheeler OEM; peak production targeted within FY27, sourcing from Greater Noida and Pantnagar.
Chassis, battery trays and metal components for an emerging EV player; supplies expected to start Q3 of the fiscal year.
Management declined to give plant-level utilisation or break-even timelines for new plants (Chennai, Pune, Bhiwandi).
Over 850 robots deployed across the company; medium-term vision is a large integrated aerospace and defence facility in India.
demand_pricing: Sector saw strong Q4 growth, helped by the GST rate cut late last year; management hopes for structural rather than pull-forward demand.
Back-to-back raw material pricing model passes steel and plastic cost changes to customers with a lag, limiting margin impact.

Q4 headwinds: oil-crisis-related supply chain disruption, higher raw material, energy and logistics costs, and Haryana minimum wage increase. Fuel and labour costs expected to be passed on over time; transport cost recovery still under discussion with key OEMs.
Two-wheeler segment only recently returned to pre-COVID peak; management sees long-term headroom.
Aerospace demand described as very strong, with OEM order backlogs of 8-10+ years; qualification cycles of 12-24 months cited as the main barrier.
Chester Hall: rejection rate 0.5%-1%; advanced discussions to transfer part of its subcontracted work to India.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins trend through the quarters, and how will the company absorb commodity, fuel and labour cost pressures to hold full-year margins stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 was hit by the INR94.7 mn one-time aerospace loss and acquisition fees, both called one-time. Fuel and labour costs to be passed on over time; transport costs still under discussion. Full-year guidance maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How large can the two new two-wheeler OEM customers become over two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects both to become very large over 2-3 years, with content per vehicle rising sharply and cross-model penetration. The Japanese OEM order is about INR200 crore annually, and the Bangalore program is one of the sharpest ramp-ups in three years.

qa_highlights.question: How much can aerospace contribute in four to five years, and can manufacturing move to India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets aerospace above 10% of revenue and sees India as a best-cost base. It is in talks with OEMs to shift Chester Hall subcontracted work and new orders from Europe to India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the QIP of INR2,000 crore for?
qa_highlights.answer: Only an enabling resolution has been approved; no specific use was given, and management will update when there is progress.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive edge in exhaust systems, and what margin is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Edge comes from automation (850+ robots), high verticalisation, NVH engineering and stainless-steel plating capability. Management corrected the INR400 crore figure: the orders are INR220 crore and INR90 crore, about INR310 crore peak combined. No margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How will R&D spend scale with aerospace and steering/high-tensile products?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is included within the 6%-6.5% capex range. The R&D team has more than 163 people. Management directionally agreed on hiring and partnerships but gave no specific target.

qa_highlights.question: Will the trading business be localised, spun off or hived off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not commented on hiving off the trading business and will update later.

qa_highlights.question: Does suspension have passenger vehicle customers, and what are suspension and H-One revenue and PAT figures?
qa_highlights.answer: No PV customers yet; the suspension business serves only two- and three-wheeler OEMs, with four marquee customers, three onboarded in the last 18 months. Management did not have suspension, polymer or H-One revenue and PAT figures and will follow up offline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inorganic strategy for FY27, and what are the content per vehicle and plant utilisation trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets are chosen on customers, capabilities and verticalisation at mild valuations (book value to mid-single-digit EV/EBITDA); all four acquisitions are EPS and ROCE accretive. Content per vehicle has risen 60-65% in two-wheelers and is 40-45% in four-wheelers and CVs. Plant utilisation and break-even were not disclosed.

risks_watch: Margin trajectory: management guides FY26-level EBITDA margins (12.1%) but Q4 EBITDA margin was 11.4%; watch whether the one-time INR94.7 mn aerospace loss and acquisition fees recur or fade in Q1 FY27.
Oil-crisis cost pass-through: fuel and labour costs to be passed on over time, transport cost recovery still under discussion with key OEMs; a lag in recovery could compress margins.

Execution of new programmes: Bangalore brownfield (production from Q2 FY27), Japanese OEM exhaust/metal order (production from Q4 FY26-27), Haridwar ramp to peak within FY27, and EV-player chassis supplies from Q3; monitor ramp timing.
Aerospace: SDM expected EBITDA positive in 2027; Chester Hall transfer of subcontracted work to India is in advanced talks but not yet signed; qualification cycles of 12-24 months.

Capital and disclosure gaps: QIP of INR2,000 mn-equivalent (INR2,000 crore) approved only as an enabling resolution with no use specified; plant-level utilisation and break-even not disclosed; suspension, polymer and H-One standalone revenue and PAT to follow offline; trading business hive-off undecided.
key_quotes: Our first commitment was to deliver mid -teens revenue growth while keeping our EBITDA margins stable. And I am glad to share that we achieved this.
We expect this loss to be one -time and expect SDM to be EBITDA positive in the year 2027.
At this point of time, it's only an enabling resolution.
We are unable to comment on plant-specific questions on utilization and break-even.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the headline commitments (mid-teens growth, stable margins, 4W/CV doubling, content-per-vehicle gains), with management repeatedly calling Q4 hits one-time. Evasive on specifics: declined plant utilisation and break-even, QIP use, trading business hive-off, H-One and suspension figures, and R&D hiring targets, deferring these to later updates.

growth.why: Management guides mid-teens revenue growth for FY27 (midpoint 15%), held from prior, backed by order book and specific capacity coming live (Bangalore expansion, Haridwar ramp-up, EV supply from Q3), though plant-level utilisation and new-plant break-even timelines were not disclosed.
